Tesla stops selling every Cybertruck except the $109,990 Cyberbeast

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (812 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.
  • The Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator highlights today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.

The Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected. So the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today costs $109,990, up 57% from $69,990 in early August.

Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator highlights today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.

In a recent development, A week ago, the Cyberbeast cost $102,490. Before that, it was $99,990. That’s a $10,000 (10%) increase in about a week on a truck that hasn’t changed: 320 miles of estimated range, 11,000 lbs of towing, and 0-60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

Industry observers note that on November 6, the same day Elon Musk announced the end of Cybertruck production, Tesla raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. That made the $92,490 Premium AWD the entry point. Now it’s gone too, with no announcement. The configurator just stopped letting you pick it.

It has been revealed that newly introduced inventory isn’t an alternative either. When we checked, Tesla’s inventory search highlighted no new Cybertrucks within 200 miles of Los Angeles.

This comes two days after Musk extended Cybertruck production through the end of summer 2027 to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” On Monday, he claimed the order rate “far exceeds” production and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”.

Recent findings suggest that if there really is a backlog, cutting off the two cheaper trims is one way to cap it before the line shuts down. It also pushes whatever demand is left toward the most expensive, highest-margin version of the truck.

But the sales data doesn’t describe a truck with a demand problem in the other direction. We estimate Tesla delivered 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks in Q3, a pace of about 30,000 a year on a line with more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. And in February, Tesla was offering a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.”.

That’s $50,000 less than the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today. Nine months later.

Some of those $59,990 buyers are still waiting on delivery dates pushed into 2027. Tesla hasn’t stated whether their orders, or any other Dual Motor and Premium orders in the queue, will be built before production ends.

Unlike the thousands of $59k CT orders that may never get manufactured I can guarantee that every high margin $110k CyberBeast order will be delivered before production ends.

Sources indicate that this is the wind-down playbook, and it’s moving faster than I expected. Announce the end, raise prices, pull the cheaper trims, and sell the last trucks in their most expensive form. Tesla is squeezing as much as it can out of every remaining Cybertruck.

Recent findings suggest that I don’t blame Tesla for wanting margin on a program it’s walking away from. But it makes the “order backlog” talk look like what we stated it was: an end-of-life rush Tesla created by announcing the end, now being monetized with a $109,990 sticker. Not great for anyone who was told in 2019 that this truck would start at $39,900, or that the tri-motor version would cost $69,900.

If you want a Cybertruck that isn’t a Cyberbeast, you’re now shopping used. And I’d keep an eye on used prices, because a truck that’s going out of production with no cheaper upcoming option could hold its value better than it has over the last two years.

  • Here is our list of the top 8 decentralized exchanges in the space that users can trade on:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, decentralised exchanges, or DEXs, use smart contracts or liquidity pools to facilitate cryptocurrency trading. Owners are at the core of DEXs, as they retain complete control over their assets and do not need to depend on centralized exchanges to protect their funds or process their withdrawals. DEXs let users maintain ownership of their private keys and also reduce the risk of custody failures.

Here is our list of the top 8 decentralized exchanges in the space that users can trade on:.

Pancake or PancakeSwap is one of the most popular DEXs on the BNB Chain and was created to provide customers with a low-cost, accessible alternative to Ethereum-based decentralized exchanges.

The platform recently rebranded from PancakeSwap to Pancake, dropping “Swap” as it expanded from a single-chain token-swap DEX to a multi-chain liquidity hub spanning 11+ blockchains, and added perpetual futures and 24/7 tokenized stocks and ETFs.

Uniswap introduced the Automated Market Maker (AMM) model that changed how cryptocurrency trading could take place without any central intermediaries or traditional order books. People could swap tokens directly from their wallets across Ethereum and other blockchains.

The platform also allows users to earn rewards through peer-to-peer trading, and the open-source architecture has influenced others in the space, making it an important reference point for the DEX industry.

Raydium leverages Solana’s high-speed blockchain infrastructure, combining AMM, liquidity infrastructure, and token trading functionality. This is useful not just for DeFi consumers but also for retail users.

Customers can trade and exchange their assets directly through their wallets. The tools on Raydium help latest projects establish liquidity and attract traders. RAY is the native token of the platform and is useful with governance and incentives on the platform.

Sources indicate that hyperliquid has an order book that runs on-chain instead of an AMM, giving customers a centralized experience. The platform is especially known for its perpetual futures and spot trading services, whereas the ecosystem itself supports borrowing, lending, and real-world assets.

The platform is a Layer 1 chain and consists of 2 main components: HyperCore and HyperEVM. HyperBFT is the consensus mechanism used underneath to support both. Stop, limit, and margin orders are all supported on Hyperliquid. HYPE is the native token of the platform.

According to recent reports, balancer is a DEX protocol built on Ethereum that supports multi-token liquidity pools and yield-bearing assets. Token pairings can be customized with multiple assets, unlike the traditional 50/50 pairings. It functions more like an automated portfolio manager, customizing token weights, creating pools with adjustable weight ratios, and letting users set their own trading fee.

The platform provides a level of flexibility that lets users and liquidity providers create specialized trading environments and program them as per their needs.

According to recent reports, sushiSwap was introduced as a fork of Uniswap in 2020 and lets owners trade through liquidity pools instead of traditional order books. These users can either be Traders or Swappers or users who want to exchange one cryptocurrency for another; or Liquidity Providers who supply assets to liquidity pools to conduct trades.

It has been revealed that the platform uses a multichain approach and supports various blockchain networks, letting people access different DeFi environments. The native token of the platform is SUSHI, which is useful in governance and incentive-based applications.

Orca lets users swap and conduct transactions at lightning fast speeds. Whirlpools are the platform’s concentrated liquidity pools that let liquidity providers provide capital within selected price ranges instead of distributing it uniformly across a price curve.

Industry observers note that orca is the native token of the platform. The platform’s simple interface appeals to a lot of traders. Wallet-to-wallet trading of SPL tokens is also a viable option for people.

According to recent reports, meteora is a liquidity protocol built on Solana focusing on providing advanced liquidity management and supporting token swaps. Dynamic Liquidity Market Maker or DLMM is a major feature of the platform allowing liquidity providers to allocate assets across different price bins.

Liquidity providers get to concentrate their assets around selected trading prices and various liquidity pool configurations can accomodate various market conditions and trading strategies. Meteora also supports emerging token projects and liquidity tools that can be helpful to establish trading markets and manage liquidity.

Decentralised exchanges are an essential part of the crypto and DeFi ecosystem. DEX platforms give people an extra level of control over their assets when they buy, sell, exchange or manage their assets.

In a recent development, while every trader has their own requirements, the best platform would depend upon individual needs, preferred networks, trading pairs and risks. Users should do their own research before investing.

The Shiba Inu ecosystem may be set for a privacy boost, as longtime SHIB community member and developer Mazrael hints at privacy potential coming to the blockchain.

Shiba Inu's privacy potential draws from Oxbow's Privacy Pools, the privacy design coauthored by Ethereum cofounder Vitalik Buterin, which is presently a plug-in in the Ethereum Foundation's Kohaku wallet SDK.Mazrael noted that Shibarium is now ready for Oxbow's Privacy Pools, with the groundwork already being done.

In a recent development, WOOF 🐶🪖🫡 And it's privacy done the regulation-friendly way. Privacy Pools come from a 2023 paper Vitalik co-wrote: deposits are screened, so stolen funds can't hide in the crowd, while honest customers stay private. No KYC, no backdoors, and you can always exit publicly. Two ways to bring it to Shibarium: 0xbow deploys it themselves, or the community deploys the same contracts and runs a relayer. Shibarium is ready either way, and ShibWallet already runs it on testnet 🔥.

The groundwork done on Shibarium (Chain ID 109) includes Cancun opcodes, BN254 pairing support for zero-knowledge proofs, CreateX and Arachnid factories and verified PoseidonT3 and PoseidonT4 contracts at Ethereum addresses.

Mazrael shared a GitHub document, "Shibarium (chain 109) support: chain is prepared," which highlighted this fact. Addressed to the Oxbow team was a request: "Hi 0xbow team! We build on Shibarium (chain ID 109) and would love to see Privacy Pools there. We've done the groundwork so a deployment would be as easy as possible, and ShibWallet plans to integrate it through Kohaku from day one.".

Mazrael explained that Privacy Pools originated from a 2023 paper Ethereum cofounder Vitalik coauthored: deposits are screened, so stolen funds can't hide in the crowd, while honest customers stay private. No KYC, no backdoors and users can always exit publicly.

Two ways to bring it to Shibarium include 0xbow deploys it themselves, or the community deploys the same contracts and runs a relayer.

For the first option, Mazrael has relayed a GitHub request to the Oxbow team, which is right now showing signs of a green light, with Mazrael remarking that "they did the approval thing when we posted basically.".

A 0xbow privacy pool deployment for Shiba Inu will bring 'entry point', 'verifiers', and 'PrivacyPoolSimple' for native BONE (Shibarium's gas token). It will also bring 'PrivacyPoolComplex' for SHIB and other ecosystem tokens later.

The Shib ecosystem would become privacy-complian and ShibWallet would integrate it through Kohaku from day one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Bitcoin put can cushion losses for its buyer, while the trades a dealer makes to hedge the same option can make a fresh selloff harder to stop.

In its Nov. 24 report, Glassnode estimated that options dealers could reinforce declines by selling and rallies by buying when Bitcoin traded between $58,000 and $64,000. The US inflation report due Nov. 25 gives that setup a near-term test.

Recent findings suggest that on a seven-day average, 1.7 Bitcoin puts traded for every call, the highest ratio since June 2022, according to Glassnode’s Nov. 24 report.

It has been revealed that the put-to-call ratio for outstanding contracts separately reached its highest since May 2021. Put trading includes sellers and positions that serve purposes beyond crash protection, so the volume ratio demonstrates where activity shifted without revealing who took which side.

It has been revealed that A put gives its buyer the right to sell at a fixed price, or receive the equivalent cash payoff. The lower Bitcoin finishes below that price, the larger the payoff before the option's cost.

A dealer who sells the put takes the other side of that exposure and can hedge by selling Bitcoin or futures. As Bitcoin falls, the put becomes more sensitive to the decline, and the dealer may need to sell more to keep the hedge balanced.

Industry observers note that gamma measures how swiftly an option’s price sensitivity changes. If prices reverse, a dealer in short gamma can buy back part of the hedge, adding to the rebound.

The feedback can be stronger when few buyers or sellers stand ready to take the other side, a pattern that researchers studying equity options found in less liquid stocks.

Industry observers note that glassnode estimated positive dealer gamma in the adjoining $56,000-$58,000 and $64,000-$66,000 bands. Dealers hedging positive gamma can buy weakness and sell strength, helping absorb a move. Those were modeled zones for one snapshot, and new trades or expiries can shift them.

Industry observers note that A separate estimate from GEX Monitor from Nov. 24 also revealed negative net gamma near $60,000, with the largest concentration by absolute exposure at that strike.

According to recent reports, glassnode’s Nov. 24 estimate put short gamma between $58,000 and $64,000. Bitcoin was near $59,700 later that day.

Within the estimated short-gamma band, dealer hedges can reinforce both a selloff and a rally.

The bands describe an estimate at one point in time. Dealer positions, liquidity and the influence of hedging can change as prices move, trades arrive or contracts expire.

Range widths are proportional to the reported dollar spans. Glassnode’s estimates use Nov. 24 data at 16:00 UTC. The later CryptoSlate observation at 21:12 UTC is rounded to $59,700. The paths illustrate short-gamma dealers hedging a move.

Industry observers note that the bands describe an estimate at one point in time. Dealer positions, liquidity and the influence of hedging can change as prices move, trades arrive or contracts expire.

Sources indicate that glassnode estimated that nearly 90% of the leveraged futures longs it had flagged between the prior week’s Bitcoin price and its realized price had cleared. Realized price is the average price at which coins last moved.

The selloff had already pushed into a $55,000-$62,000 cluster of positions at risk of liquidation.

Futures liquidations occur when traders can no longer meet their margin requirements, so options dealers rebalance as prices move even if nobody faces a margin call.

Glassnode reported $4.3 billion of net outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs over the 20 trading days covered in the report.

It has been revealed that the Bureau of Economic Analysis scheduled its October inflation report and revised third-quarter GDP for Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The inflation report includes the personal consumption expenditures price index (PCE).

Trading Economics listed a 0.3% monthly consensus for core PCE, which excludes food and energy. The Cleveland Fed’s model estimated 0.27% separately.

Investors are watching what the data means for rates after the Fed’s October minutes showed broad support for more tightening if the economy evolved as officials expected.

At derivatives exchange Deribit, Wednesday’s daily Bitcoin options are scheduled to expire at 3 a.m. ET, five and a half hours before the release.

Recent findings suggest that they had about 6,172 BTC of open interest, around 1.4% of outstanding coin-settled Bitcoin options on Deribit, in Deribit’s Nov. 24 options data, against 111,797 BTC in the Nov. 27 monthly expiry.

In a recent development, deribit’s Nov. 24 coin-settled Bitcoin options book indicated 6,172 BTC of gross open interest in the daily expiry before PCE and 111,797 BTC in the monthly expiry after it. The exchange publishes open interest with an eight-hour lag.

Source: Deribit options data · Deribit expiry policy · Deribit public API changelog · BEA release schedule.

CryptoSlate estimated the effect of removing Wednesday’s expiry using coin-settled contracts expiring within 30 days.

Assuming dealers held the long side of every call and the short side of every put, contracts set to outlast the release accounted for about 93% of the Nov. 24 model’s net negative gamma.

Recent findings suggest that the Nov. 27 expiry alone accounted for about 49% of the original total, leaving about 7% in Wednesday’s expiry under the same assumptions.

The calculation holds prices and positions at their Nov. 24 readings, so actual gamma can shift as Bitcoin moves and expiry approaches, and the public exchange data counts contracts without identifying dealer positions.

In a recent development, the Nov. 27 put open interest was spread across several strikes, including $60,000, $63,000 and $64,000. At the same $60,000 strike, annualized implied volatility was 50.4% for Wednesday’s expiry, 56.1% for Thursday’s and 54.6% for Friday’s.

The higher Thursday and Friday marks cover the inflation release and other risks over longer periods.

A hot print could lift rate expectations and start a selloff that short-gamma dealers reinforce with hedge sales.

A cool print could ease rate pressure and prompt a rebound that the same dealers reinforce by buying. If inflation comes in close to forecasts, the GDP figures and demand for Bitcoin could matter more.

According to recent reports, for the rest of the week, watch whether Friday’s expiry changes positioning and whether spot buyers return. The NYSE closes for Thanksgiving, ending Friday’s core equity session at 1 p.m. ET.

If dealers turn long gamma or liquidity improves enough to absorb their trades, the same catalyst could produce a smaller swing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Cryptopedia » Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use.

Compare the top hardware and software crypto wallets to find your safest, easiest self-custody setup.

Industry observers note that keeping your cryptocurrency on an exchange is convenient, but it comes with risks. If the exchange gets hacked, freezes withdrawals, or runs into financial trouble, accessing your funds can become difficult. Using a self-custody wallet gives you direct control over your private keys and, ultimately, your crypto.

Whether you are holding Bitcoin for the next decade, trading memecoins on Solana, or exploring decentralized finance (DeFi), choosing the right wallet matters. Some wallets are designed to keep your assets as secure as possible, while others make it easier to trade, manage tokens, and connect to Web3 apps.

To help you find the right option, we’ve put together a list of seven popular crypto wallets, covering what each one does best, its main advantages, and what to consider before choosing it.

*Prices change frequently, so always confirm on the manufacturer’s official website.

If your primary goal is long-term wealth preservation, Ledger remains the industry benchmark for cold storage.

Unlike mobile apps that stay connected to the internet, Ledger devices store your private keys inside an offline, certified Secure Element chip, the same class of chip used in passports and credit cards (check Ledger’s website for the current certification details).

Through the Ledger Live companion app, you can buy, swap, and stake thousands of coins and tokens. Your private keys never leave the device. Ledger Live runs on your connected phone or computer, but transactions are signed on the Ledger itself.

Industry observers note that for those who live by the motto “don’t trust, verify,” Trezor is the gold standard. Contrary to the competitors that keep parts of their code proprietary, Trezor’s firmware is fully open-source, meaning independent security researchers constantly audit it for vulnerabilities.

The Trezor Safe 5 pairs this transparency with a vibrant color touchscreen, haptic feedback, and an EAL6+ Secure Element. It also offers a dedicated Bitcoin-only firmware option for maximalists who want to minimize attack surfaces.

When it comes to interacting with decentralized applications (DApps), decentralized exchanges (DEXs), and NFT marketplaces, MetaMask is the undisputed gateway to Web3.

Available as both a browser extension and a mobile app, MetasMask connects seamlessly to virtually every Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) network, including Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base, and BNB Chain.

Modern updates have expanded MetaMask beyond Ethereum via MetaMask Snaps and allow consumers to add support for non-EVM ecosystems like Bitcoin and Solana directly inside the same interface.

Sources indicate that originally built as the flagship wallet for the Solana ecosystem, Phantom has evolved into one of the fastest, cleanest multi-chain wallets on the market. Today, it seamlessly supports Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, and Bitcoin in a single unified interface.

Recent findings suggest that what sets Phantom apart is user experience. Transaction simulations show you exact balance changes before you hit approve, and its automated spam filter hides malicious airdrop NFTs so beginners don’t accidentally click phishing links.

If you want one smartphone app that holds virtually every cryptocurrency in existence without manual network configuration, Trust Wallet is built for you.

Supporting over 100 blockchains and millions of digital assets, it removes the technical friction of adding custom RPC networks or hunting down token contract addresses.

It also includes a built-in Web3 browser, straightforward in-app staking for major proof-of-stake coins, and an integrated Security Scanner that flags risky smart contracts.

Recent findings suggest that many newcomers confuse the main Coinbase exchange app with Coinbase Wallet, but they are completely separate products. Coinbase Wallet is a true non-custodial wallet—meaning you hold your own 12-word recovery phrase, and Coinbase cannot freeze or access your funds.

Recent findings suggest that note that the app’s branding has changed recently: Coinbase renamed it “Base App” in July 2025 and restored the Coinbase Wallet name in September 2026. It has since shifted toward multichain trading, including perpetual futures, prediction markets, and tokenized stocks, so some of its features are now aimed at more active traders.

Its biggest advantage is frictionless onboarding. You can link your exchange account to transfer funds into self-custody in seconds, claim a free human-readable username instead of copying long hexadecimal addresses, and explore Base and Ethereum DApps.

Traditional hardware wallets require cables, batteries, and carefully guarding a 24-word paper backup. Tangem reimagines cold storage as a sleek, waterproof smart card—roughly the size and thickness of a standard bank debit card.

To approve a transaction, you simply tap the card against the back of your NFC-enabled smartphone. Tangem comes in sets of two or three cards that act as physical backups for one another, allowing you to skip vulnerable paper seed phrases entirely (though a traditional seed option is still available if you prefer it).

Understanding the difference between hot and cold storage saves you from overpaying—or worse, leaving your funds exposed:.

It has been revealed that A common rule of thumb among experienced crypto investors is to use both, for example keeping around 90% of long-term holdings in a cold wallet and about 10% in a hot wallet for everyday trading and Web3 exploration. This is a guideline, not a standard – adjust it to your own situation.

According to recent reports, with crypto, there’s no bank to call if something goes wrong. Transactions are usually irreversible, and if an exchange freezes withdrawals or goes bankrupt, your funds could be stuck for months or even years.

According to recent reports, that’s why choosing the best crypto wallet matters. It gives you more control over your money and lets you manage your funds without relying on an exchange.

Your cryptocurrency is not stored inside the physical device—it lives on the blockchain. If your Ledger, Trezor, or Tangem card is lost, stolen, or broken, you can buy a replacement device and restore full access to your funds in minutes using your 12- or 24-word recovery phrase (or backup Tangem card).

According to recent reports, while no system is 100% immune, cold hardware wallets cannot be hacked remotely because your private keys stay offline. Most wallet “hacks” happen when customers accidentally sign a malicious smart contract on a phishing website or store their seed phrase digitally where malware can find it.

Software wallets like MetaMask, Phantom, and Trust Wallet are completely free to download and hold crypto in. Hardware wallets require an upfront purchase (typically $55 to $250). Regardless of the wallet you choose, you will still pay standard blockchain network (“gas”) fees whenever you send or swap tokens.

Recent findings suggest that with a custodial wallet (like a standard exchange account), a third-party company holds your private keys and can freeze or restrict your withdrawals. With a non-custodial (self-custody) wallet, only you hold the private keys—meaning nobody can block your transactions, though you are solely responsible for backing up your recovery phrase.

It has been revealed that no. Unlike traditional bank accounts, funds in a self-custody crypto wallet are not covered by government deposit insurance like the FDIC or SIPC. Because you act as your own bank, protecting your recovery phrase and verifying transaction details before approving them is your primary safeguard.

Recent findings suggest that the short-term holder spent output profit ratio (STH SOPR) was at 0.99. Readings below 1.0 meant coins of this group are, on average, moving at a loss.

Sources indicate that an SOPR return above 1.0 would signal the cohort’s profitability. Yet, the 22-day below-break-even LTH SOPR streak, alongside the BTC weakness and lack of demand, was a worrisome signal.

Alphractal data showed that the onchain realized price of Bitcoin was $53,104. If these bearish conditions persist, a price drop to $53k could materialize.

In the second half of his post, McGlone argued that the strong annual gains previously seen in Bitcoin, natural gas, gold, silver and other commodities would reverse and spread weakness into the broader stock market, potentially leaving the S&P 500 with its third annual decline since 2009.

Industry observers note that he anticipates significant drawdowns that began from early October highs, lower prices for crude oil and copper, a shift by the Federal Reserve toward easing, and a normal post-inflation period of deflation as US housing peaks. Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on the SSP

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (648 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.
  • As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.
  • The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

According to recent reports, “We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer said in the memo reviewed by Reuters. The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer confirmed earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.

According to Autocar, Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

It has been revealed that production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

BMW has the new i3, and Mercedes-Benz has the C-Class EV, both of which feature major improvements in range, charging, and efficiency over their previous-generation EVs.

Volkswagen said in 2023 that the 800V SSP will serve as a “single future backbone with integrated electric and electronics architecture,” claiming that more than 40 million models were expected to be built on it.

The firm also said investment and R&D costs were expected to be reduced by about 30% compared to the current MEB platform, enabling most models “to achieve the same margin compared to their conventionally powered counterparts.”.

Volkswagen’s software struggles started in its internal division, Cariad, leading to delays, missed targets, and budget overruns.

To fix it, VW turned to Rivian, forming a joint venture to develop its next-gen software-defined vehicle (SDV) electrical architecture.

In March, VW noted several test vehicles, including the ID.EVERY1, Audi, and Scout with the SDV architecture underwent “comprehensive evaluation,” and successfully validated over-the-air (OTA) functionality.

Being cash efficient is good, but delays to the next-gen platform that will keep you competitive with rival brands seem like a problem.

Heavy ETF outflows, surging put bets, and fragile support leave traders watching whether a deeper slide is just beginning.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 on Wednesday, trading at around $58,220 as concerns about further losses grew ahead of Thanksgiving. The BTC price dropped 2.8% in 24 hours following the release of October inflation data, which demonstrated that price pressures remained elevated according to the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure.

It has been revealed that the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that the October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% in October, matching September’s increase.

Recent findings suggest that core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed 0.3% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier. Headline PCE inflation increased 3.8% from a year earlier.

According to recent reports, the report also revealed that US personal income rose 0.7% in October, while consumer spending increased 0.3%. However, real consumer spending was virtually unchanged, suggesting that higher prices continued to weigh on purchasing power.

Bitcoin price fell to about $55,300 over the weekend before recovering to around $64,400 on Tuesday on renewed stock market optimism after Nvidia reinstated its CEO, Jensen Huang.

However, the major crypto “acted as the canary in the coal mine”, according to Glassnode: BTC fully gave back the NVIDIA-driven rally within hours while stocks lagged, then came under pressure. Price broke the $62,000–66,000 support zone, retested summer lows, and is struggling to hold around the $60,000 level.

Bitcoin lost nearly 26% of its value over the past 30 days, and the realized losses are the heaviest since the FTX crash in November 2022.

In addition to that, approximately 90% of the tracked leveraged long positions between the previous week’s market price and Bitcoin’s realized price ($53,200) have been liquidated.

Glassnode suggests that much of the selling pressure is coming from the US. Over the past 20 trading days, US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen around $4.3 billion in net outflows, marking one of their biggest periods of withdrawals since launch.

Spot market activity tells a similar story: over the past 30 days, US investors on Coinbase have been net sellers, while buying and selling on Binance have remained relatively balanced.

According to recent reports, glassnode’s latest data highlights growing bearishness among Bitcoin options traders, with limited support against sharp price movements around current levels. Between $58K and $64K, options dealers are positioned in a way that could amplify volatility, potentially accelerating a sell-off if prices fall further.

Meanwhile, bearish bets are rising. Traders bought 1.7 put options for every call last week, the highest ratio since June 2022. Similar levels of pessimism appeared near Bitcoin’s 2022 market low, although prices continued falling for several more months.

Glassnode warns that Bitcoin’s current decline may not be over. Bitcoin price remains weaker than traditional equities, US buying demand is lacking, and the market is struggling to hold its summer lows.

Sources indicate that glassnode identifies $60,000 as a key level to watch. A decisive break below it, followed by a close under $58,500, could open the door to a decline towards $53,200.

A recovery above $60,000, supported by renewed spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, would offer stronger evidence that the market is stabilising.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin exchange reserves have declined by approximately 42,000 BTC over the past month as the cryptocurrency struggles around $60,000.

The reduction comes as Bitcoin deposits and withdrawals across centralized trading platforms reached their highest levels since February, according to CryptoQuant data.

Exchange reserves fell from approximately 2.889 million BTC to 2.847 million BTC during a period in which Bitcoin's price declined roughly 26%, from $80,700 to $59,600.

The reduction approaches 50,000 BTC when measured from the Oct. 26 peak in exchange reserves.

It has been revealed that A Nov. 24 analysis by CryptoQuant contributor CryptoOnchain showed that daily Bitcoin deposits averaged 46,900 BTC over the seven days through Nov. 23, up 40.8% from the preceding week. Withdrawals increased even faster, rising 50.2% to 49,200 BTC daily.

According to recent reports, both figures reached their highest levels since Feb. 11, when Bitcoin traded near $67,048, approximately 9% above its Nov. 23 closing price of $61,195.

Bitcoin transfers through wallets tracked by CryptoQuant.

Withdrawals edged ahead even as deposits rose to a nine-month high.

Transfers between two tracked venues can count on both sides. The gross figures are rounded, and CryptoOnchain’s report does not list every venue.

Recent findings suggest that the gross bar adds CryptoOnchain’s rounded daily averages of 46,900 BTC in and 49,200 BTC out. The net bar uses its separately reported outflow of 2,369 BTC on the same scale. 2,369 divided by 96,100 is about 2.5%. All figures cover the seven days through Nov. 23, 2026.

According to recent reports, transfers between two tracked venues can count on both sides. The gross figures are rounded, and CryptoOnchain’s report does not list every venue.

According to recent reports, rising exchange deposits typically signal potential selling pressure, as investors move coins onto platforms where they can readily liquidate their holdings. Conversely, withdrawals can reduce the supply available for immediate sale.

The latest surge in activity left exchanges with average daily net withdrawals of 2,369 BTC, reversing estimated daily net inflows of roughly 550 BTC during the preceding week.

Binance accounted for approximately 60% of those net withdrawals, despite representing just 19% of combined exchange flows.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant's exchange whale ratio, which measures the share of deposits attributable to the 10 largest inflows, declined 8.4% week over week to 22.52%.

The recent contraction in exchange reserves contrasts with the buildup that preceded Bitcoin's sharp decline earlier this month.

Recent findings suggest that between Nov. 8 and 11, exchange balances increased by approximately 15,000 BTC while Bitcoin traded between $74,000 and $75,000. The cryptocurrency subsequently fell to around $64,000.

Since Nov. 13, however, exchange reserves and Bitcoin's price have declined together, suggesting that existing exchange inventories may be supplying part of the market's selling pressure.

The latest surge in transfers also reflects potential changes in how Bitcoin is distributed across trading platforms.

As CryptoSlate previously reported, approximately 11,028 BTC moved from Coinbase- and Binance-linked addresses to Kraken on Nov. 21.

Such transfers can increase reported exchange activity without adding to aggregate reserves.

With fewer coins held across tracked exchanges, a recovery in demand could encounter a smaller pool of readily available Bitcoin.

However, exchange reserves have registered a modest increase over the past two days. Another buildup resembling the 15,000 BTC increase earlier this month could signal renewed selling pressure as Bitcoin attempts to defend $60,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that bitcoin [BTC] ETFs faced their worst month since launch, recording approximately $4.94 billion in Net Outflows during November so far. With several days still left, the month had already overtaken June’s $4.51 billion withdrawal.

Yet institutional ownership data offered a different perspective. Billions were leaving the funds, while reported institutional exposure remained substantial.

In a recent development, just for a quick recap, the year started weak. January recorded $1.61 billion in Net Outflows, followed by $206.52 million in February.

Industry observers note that A brief recovery followed. March attracted $1.32 billion in Net Inflows, while April brought another $1.97 billion. May, however, recorded $2.43 billion in Net Outflows. June followed with $4.51 billion, making it the year’s second-worst month.

In a recent development, july’s $172.43 million in Net Inflows offered a near-flat pause before a stronger rebound. August attracted $3.52 billion, followed by $2.65 billion in September. That recovery unravelled in October, when $515.03 million left the funds. November’s $4.94 billion withdrawal then pushed the year towards another low.

In fact, Glassnode also pointed out that Bitcoin ETF trading volume has fallen below its median since launch.

In a recent development, hence, the persistent selling pressure has raised concerns about institutional confidence in Bitcoin. This is because a closer look at institutional ownership data suggests that Wall Street is not abandoning Bitcoin ETFs just yet.

In fact, institutional participation has continued to expand despite the deteriorating market sentiment, raising an key question: What is keeping institutions invested in Bitcoin ETFs when investors are pulling billions out of them?

According to Bloomberg ETF analyst James Seyffart, 2,223 institutional filers collectively reported approximately $29.77 billion in Bitcoin ETF exposure, equivalent to 356,072 BTC.

In a recent development, investment advisors accounted for the largest share, with 1,863 filers holding approximately 160,195 BTC worth $13.39 billion. Brokerage firms followed with 59,255 BTC, while hedge funds held approximately 58,088 BTC. Banks and trusts also have considerable exposure, holding 28,937 BTC and 19,723 BTC, respectively.

More importantly, the data demonstrates that institutional ownership increased by 56,493 BTC over the one-year period. Well, according to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions have also added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.

It has been revealed that this suggests that the recent outflow streak has not translated into a complete institutional retreat. In this, Wells Fargo has emerged as a major institutional holder, with its aggregated filings showing approximately 30,549 BTC in exposure.

Jane Street, Goldman Sachs, Millennium Management, and Morgan Stanley were also featured among the notable holders. However, the current selling pressure cannot be overlooked.

According to recent reports, ecoinometrics noted that November’s ETF flow trajectory was closely following its bearish simulation. Therefore, if the trend continues, its model suggests Bitcoin could potentially revisit the low-$50,000 range.

Zcash holders just got a upcoming update as the major crypto exchange Gemini has announced support for Shielded Zcash deposits.

Scott Merkel, 'Wolf of All Streets,' shared this upgrade in an X post, highlighting the milestone as the first of its kind for any major exchange. According to Merkel, Gemini now lets customers deposit Zcash (ZEC) to shielded addresses, saying it is the first major exchange with both shielded deposits and withdrawals.

GEMINI NOW LETS CUSTOMERS DEPOSIT ZCASH $ZEC TO SHIELDED ADDRESSES, SAYING IT IS THE FIRST MAJOR EXCHANGE WITH BOTH SHIELDED DEPOSITS AND WITHDRAWALS https://t.co/d9pIFJ6uJM.

Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss shared the milestone in a recent X post, adding that the recent move builds on the launch of shielded Zcash withdrawals on Gemini this summer.

In July 2026, shortly after the Ironwood upgrade was activated, Gemini launched support for shielded Zcash withdrawals to the new Ironwood pool, allowing customers to send Zcash from Gemini to their Ironwood deposit address. Ironwood (NU6.3) went live on July 28, 2026, at block height 3,428,143, bringing a new shielded pool for Zcash.

With the recent launch of support for Shielded Zcash deposits, Gemini users can make Shielded Zcash deposits and withdrawals to and from Ironwood, with Winklevoss remarking that the private movement of money was now complete.

Zcash's total shielded supply now sits at around 4.93 million ZEC (around 28.94% of total ZEC supply) as of November 25, 2026.

Sources indicate that november has brought in key updates for the Zcash network. Zcash's NU7 upgrade went live earlier in November 2026, slashing ZEC's target block time to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The new 25-second block target lets miners add a batch of transactions to the chain three times as often.

In a recent development, none of this prints extra ZEC. Each block pays a third as much and halvings come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving.

Recent findings suggest that days after the NU7 upgrade, the Zcash Foundation followed up with the release of Zebra 7.1.0, which fixed ten security advisories, most of which closed off ways in which another node on the network (a peer) could stop a Zebra node from catching up with the chain or make it run out of memory. It also added sync and memory diagnostics, automatic peer recovery, and clearer errors.

  • NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.
  • The Latest York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role.

NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.

The Latest York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.

Her distinction: settling share ownership and moving money across currencies are separate jobs, and winning one does not automatically secure the other.

It has been revealed that according to Dr. Stevenson, Ava Labs confirmed that Avalanche would provide the core ledger for the clearing firm behind the proposed platform.

She cites Wall Street Journal reporting that Avalanche would be its sole settlement blockchain, with regulatory approval still required.

Sources indicate that the proposed venue would support around-the-clock trading and near-instant settlement. Stevenson claims NYSE tested Avalanche for roughly a year, prioritizing transaction speed, predictable costs and control over who can participate.

Industry observers note that that permissioning capability matters for a regulated exchange. Avalanche (AVAX) can support customized networks with participation restrictions, rather than requiring the exchange to conduct settlement on an unrestricted public network.

It has been revealed that AVAX rose as much as roughly 10% on the news, according to the video. Stevenson, who discloses holding the token, calls the selection a win for Avalanche, but cautions against treating infrastructure adoption as proof of investment returns.

According to recent reports, “A network being used by a massive name and its token being needed” are different things, she says. The announcement, in her account, provided neither revenue figures nor a commitment that NYSE would buy or hold AVAX.

Dr. Stevenson’s XRP thesis centers on overseas investors funding dollar-denominated stock purchases outside conventional banking hours.

A trader holding yen or another currency would need access to dollars or dollar-linked funding before buying U.S. shares.

She argues that this creates an opportunity for cross-border payment infrastructure, including XRP. But it remains a proposed use case, not a disclosed partnership: “I’m not telling you that NYSE is going to pick XRP for that.”.

The YouTube video episode does not establish that XRP would be necessary for such funding. Nor does expanded trading access, by itself, demonstrate future demand for the token.

Sources indicate that dr. Kamilah Stevenson also says the platform would support tokenized stocks issued across multiple blockchains, distinguishing asset issuance from the ledger used for settlement.

Those details matter more than a simple Avalanche-versus-XRP contest: the unresolved questions are which services institutions actually adopt, what generates revenue, and whether that activity requires either token.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China.
  • The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.
  • We knew it was coming soon after the newly introduced model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China. This five-seat flagship SUV packs more than you’d expect for the money, with two massive 30-inch-plus screens inside and up to 850 km (528 miles) of CLTC range.

The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.

We knew it was coming soon after the newly introduced model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

BYD declared on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.

The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

According to recent reports, inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.

Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.

The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD said.

Like many of its upcoming flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.

Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division said third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.

Industry observers note that why mention "two enormous screens" like they are some markers of a more premium vehicle or represent some value? We don't measure the utility of cars by screen real estate per dollar. It's the other part of the utility that matter: range, driving dynamics, road trip convenience, fit/finish/materials/insulation. Personally, I don't think "enormous screens" are going to age well as an automotive trend.

The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it launched in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.

The Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).

Sources indicate that will BYD’s smaller five-seat SUV draw the same demand? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

  • Crypto market insights provided by Unfolded revealed that the combined supply of Sky's two stablecoins, DAI and USDS, has declined 43% to $7.71 billion from a record $13.62 billion on April 5.
  • It has been revealed that DAI plus USDS circulating supply across all chains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sky, the $3.4 billion lending protocol, is facing mounting pressure across its DeFi ecosystem as a withdrawal crisis coincides with a multibillion-dollar contraction in its stablecoin supply.

Crypto market insights provided by Unfolded revealed that the combined supply of Sky's two stablecoins, DAI and USDS, has declined 43% to $7.71 billion from a record $13.62 billion on April 5.

It has been revealed that DAI plus USDS circulating supply across all chains. Mid-month readings to Oct. 2026 are approximated from Unfolded’s DefiLlama-based image and rounded to $0.25 billion. Apr. 5 ($13.62B) and Nov. 24 ($7.71B) are the source’s printed observations. No November intermediate levels are invented; the Nov. 19 one-day USDS outflow is reported separately in the source. This area chart is not a native stacked-area view.

Sources indicate that source: Unfolded, Sky DAI and USDS supply graphic (Nov. 24, 2026), sourced from DefiLlama · DefiLlama stablecoin circulating supply, all chains.

It has been revealed that USDS alone contracted by $2.03 billion on Nov. 19, losing 39% in a single day as a large holder converted the stablecoin into USDC. Its supply has now fallen 65% from its peak.

Selected monthly snapshots digitized from Unfolded’s chart, generally approximate to $0.25 billion; Nov. 24 DAI ($4.54B) and USDS ($3.17B) are rounded DefiLlama readings consistent with the $7.71B combined endpoint. Earlier pre-USDS observations show DAI only. The Apr. 5 record is excluded here because the original source gives its combined total but not exact separate DAI and USDS balances.

Source: Unfolded, Sky DAI and USDS supply graphic (Nov. 24, 2026), sourced from DefiLlama · DefiLlama stablecoin circulating supply, all chains.

The pressure extends to Sky's governance token, which rose 5% over the past 24 hours to $0.04011 but remains down 23% over the past week and 42% over the past month.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, depositors in Sky's stUSDS lending vault are struggling to access their funds. As of Nov. 24, Spark's dashboard demonstrated just 2,121 USDS available for withdrawals against 158.32 million USDS in vault assets.

The liquidity shortage centers on Sky's stUSDS product, which uses stablecoin deposits to finance loans backed by staked SKY.

DeFi analyst Ignas pointed out that the lending product operates separately from the collateral backing DAI and USDS, as well as the strategies generating returns for ordinary sUSDS savings holders.

However, the sharp decline in SKY's price has intensified concerns over loans taken out by some of the ecosystem's largest participants, particularly Sky co-founder Rune Christensen.

A Nov. 19 investigation by blockchain analytics firm Bitquery found that Christensen's associated positions were backed by 3.58 billion SKY, representing approximately 15% of the token's circulating supply.

Bitquery identified 25 borrowing transactions without a repayment on the current lending engine between May 2025 and Nov. 19, during which the positions accumulated approximately 10.4 million USDS in unpaid interest.

Three of the four identified positions also fell below their required collateralization thresholds, according to Bitquery's analysis, while automatic liquidations were disabled.

The four vaults owed 74.46 million USDS as of Nov. 24, while Sky Frontier Foundation owed another 40.17 million USDS. Their combined borrowing represents approximately 72% of the stUSDS vault's assets.

The scale of Christensen's SKY exposure complicates his repayment efforts, as selling substantial quantities on the open market could weaken the token's price and the collateral backing other loans.

On Nov. 23, Christensen remarked he was exploring a direct sale of some of his SKY holdings to institutional investors. Crypto entrepreneur Du Jun subsequently expressed interest in acquiring his entire position.

Unlike Christensen, Sky Frontier Foundation already holds stablecoin savings that could substantially reduce its borrowing.

On-chain data reviewed by CryptoSlate revealed that the foundation held approximately 27.9 million USDS in redeemable savings on Nov. 24.

Deploying those funds would allow the foundation to repay roughly 69% of its outstanding debt without selling SKY, releasing liquidity equivalent to nearly 18% of the stUSDS vault's assets.

The repayment could also substantially reduce the foundation's financing expenses.

Sources indicate that A Nov. 23 governance forum post highlighted that the foundation was paying nearly 50% in annualized borrowing costs while earning approximately 3.8% on its savings.

At those rates, repaying 27.9 million USDS would reduce the foundation's net annualized financing costs by approximately $12.8 million.

The foundation previously disclosed that it borrowed against its locked SKY holdings to finance operations, leaving it to determine how much of its savings it can commit to repayment.

However, the speed at which depositors previously drained liquidity shows how short-lived any relief could be under the vault's existing withdrawal mechanism.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 23, Christensen's wallet repaid 3 million USDS. Within 24 seconds, ten withdrawals totaling approximately the same amount followed, with the first two alone accounting for roughly 83% of the repayment.

Sky Frontier Foundation could cover much of its loan from savings. The prior repayment shows how fast cash can be withdrawn.

The foundation’s savings could cover about 69% of the loan. The stUSDS vault pays withdrawals as transactions clear against a shared balance.

Industry observers note that the repayment shown for the foundation is conditional on its deciding to deploy its savings. The observed withdrawals were paid from the shared pool and do not identify ultimate recipients or guarantee access after a future repayment.

In a recent development, use the Nov. 24 block 26,487,346 accrued debt and sUSDS maxWithdraw in USDS. Scale the debt bar using their ratio and subtract the redeemable amount for the residual. The Nov. 23 timeline shows single withdrawals in the repayment block and at +12 seconds, then the aggregate of ten withdrawals through +24 seconds. Values are rounded for display.

The repayment shown for the foundation is conditional on its deciding to deploy its savings. The observed withdrawals were paid from the shared pool and do not identify ultimate recipients or guarantee access after a future repayment.

The rapid depletion has prompted calls for a proportional withdrawal queue that would distribute returning liquidity according to depositors' holdings.

A separate governance proposal would deploy $40 million to $50 million from Sky's reserves to acquire SKY directly from borrowers and apply the proceeds toward their outstanding loans.

Neither proposal has received formal approval, while the foundation has yet to commit its savings toward repayment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Q4 alone has pushed Bitcoin several years back across multiple market metrics.

It has been revealed that bitcoin’s breakdown to $55k last week took its price back to pre-2024 U.S. elections. So, almost every increase in Bitcoin’s value since the election, even the surge to $126k, has therefore been reversed. The selloff has pushed 11.6 million BTC underwater, the highest on record.

And now, this is starting to affect the Bitcoin options market too.

In a recent development, from the data shown below, BTC options traders are turning increasingly bearish. Put option buying has accelerated to levels last witnessed during BTC’s 2022 capitulation.

Sources indicate that likewise, the put-to-call ratio has reached its highest value since 2021. These extreme readings are rare and suggest that traders are increasingly preparing for more downside.

Naturally, this raises the question: What is driving this shift in sentiment?

Industry observers note that from a market psychology perspective, Bitcoin’s [BTC] drop to multi-year lows has put growing pressure on investor profitability. With 11.6 million BTC now underwater, holding through the downturn is becoming a tougher bet, especially in the current macro environment.

Notably, nothing illustrates this better than a recent Glassnode report.

Bitcoin’s falling hashrate has put miner profitability back under pressure.

To date in 2026, MARA Holdings has sold 40,581 BTC at an average price of $74,446, amassing around $3.03 billion. Much of this sale is related to the switch by Bitcoin miners to AI. Yet, the latest figures from Glassnode indicate that there may be further strains on mining.

Bitcoin’s hashrate is presently 8% down on where it was last year, the first time there has been a yearly reduction since China banned mining in 2021. However, whereas the 2021 fall was due to regulatory factors, today’s decline is mainly due to price. The bigger concern is the timing. Just 15 months before the next BTC halving occurs, miners are already contending with reduced profit margins.

In short, Bitcoin’s continued hashrate decline reflects the growing stress across the mining sector.

Recent findings suggest that miners are already seeing reduced profitability. The upcoming halving will reduce miners’ block reward and so may exacerbate this glitch. There is therefore a greater risk that miners may “continue” to switch off hardware and sell Bitcoin to maintain cashflow.

So, for now, the falling hashrate, rising underwater supply, and bearish options positioning all suggest that the market is already preparing for a tougher phase.

Bitcoin’s falling hashrate and tighter mining margins raise fresh fears of miner capitulation.

Bearish options positioning and record-high underwater supply suggest investors are bracing for further downside.

Although the past month has seen billions of XRP transferred back to exchanges, further data demonstrates that the 4.6 billion XRP inflow is substantially lower when compared with inflows seen in October.

In October, the total XRP that flowed into exchanges throughout the month was estimated at around 6 billion XRP, suggesting that XRP selling pressure has eased compared with the previous month.

This has drawn attention across the crypto market as the price of XRP suffered larger losses this month compared with last month, sparking questions about whether investor confidence is recovering.

Volkswagen said the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).

In a recent development, the latest model will sit below the ID. Polo in Volkswagen’s Electric Urban Car Family, a lineup of compact, affordable electric cars.

A recent trademark filing with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) and the German DPMA may have just revealed the name of VW’s upcoming €20,000 EV.

Industry observers note that volkswagen filed a trademark application for the name ID. UP on October 22, 2026, with the EUIPO and DPMA, suggesting this will be the name of the upcoming electric car in 2027.

Sources indicate that the trademark follows previous reports that VW planned to revive the former Up! name as part of its shift away from its previous numerical naming scheme (ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, etc.).

Volkswagen has kept most details a secret thus far. Like the ID. Polo, the first to go on sale with an established VW nameplate, the ID. UP is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery to reduce costs.

In a recent development, the VW ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery offers a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller ID. UP will likely provide around the same, if not slightly more.

It has been revealed that volkswagen stated it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a new 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).

Industry observers note that the production version of the ID. EVERY1, expected to arrive as the ID. UP, will be one of nine upcoming models VW plans to launch by 2027.

Sources indicate that volkswagen previously said the entry-level EV will be 3,880 mm long, which would position it between the former Up! (3,600 mm) and the ID. Polo (4,053 mm). Despite its compact size, VW said the electric city car will seat four passengers and offer a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.

The VW Group’s new Electric Urban Car Family is off to a strong start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.

All models within the family are built on the MEB+ platform with a FWD powertrain, and share more than 80% of the components and tech.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen said the production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be among the first vehicles based on its zonal, software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, which it is developing through its joint venture with Rivian.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin fell to $57,470 on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected US core inflation and the announcement of upcoming tariffs intensified selling across risk assets.

The Nasdaq 100 extended its losses to 2.9%, reversing the optimism that followed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO earlier this week.

In a recent development, data released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis on Nov. 25 showed that the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.8% annually in October, its second-highest reading since April 2023.

Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, accelerated to a three-year high of 3.3%, beating economists' 3.2% forecast.

Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said the stronger-than-expected core reading demonstrated that price pressures were spreading across the economy beyond the recent energy shock.

According to recent reports, the report follows increases in both consumer and producer price inflation, with financial markets now assigning a greater than 97% probability to a quarter-point interest rate hike on Dec. 9.

That would mark the Fed's second rate increase of 2026, lifting its benchmark rate to between 4% and 4.25%. Twelve months ago, investors were anticipating three rate cuts this year.

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump's administration announced a upcoming round of proposed tariffs targeting 14 major US trading partners following an eight-month investigation into foreign industrial policies.

The measures include additional tariffs of 20% on Chinese imports, up to 35% on Vietnamese goods, and up to 25% on imports from India, Taiwan and South Korea. The European Union faces duties of up to 20%.

The announcement opens another front of uncertainty for investors already grappling with the prospect of higher borrowing costs.

André Dragosch, Bitwise's European head of research, expects this market turbulence to persist, saying:.

“Market volatility will likely stay elevated in the short term until uncertainty around inflation and the outlook for monetary policy fully resolve.”.

The deteriorating macroeconomic backdrop comes as Bitcoin investors show signs of financial distress comparable to the depths of the 2022 bear market.

Blockchain analytics firm Glassnode reported that Bitcoin's correlation with the Nasdaq 100 has climbed to its highest level since September 2022. Over the past 60 trading days, Bitcoin has consistently underperformed the index on both up and down days.

That weakness has coincided with a surge in demand for downside protection across Bitcoin's options market.

According to Glassnode, the seven-day average put-to-call trading volume ratio reached 1.7 last week, its highest level since June 2022. The corresponding ratio for outstanding options contracts climbed to its highest level since May 2021.

“The last rush into puts like this was June 2022. Bitcoin was near $20,000 in the middle of the capitulation. The final low came five months later, below $17,000.”.

Sources indicate that the growing pessimism extends beyond derivatives markets. CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju noted Bitcoin investors are underwater at historical capitulation levels, while Glassnode reported that realized losses, relative to recent capital inflows, had reached their highest level since FTX collapsed in November 2022.

Institutional demand has also weakened, with US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds registering $4.9 billion in net outflows this month.

Glassnode identified Bitcoin's realized price of $53,200 as the next major threshold should the cryptocurrency close decisively below its June closing low of $58,500.

According to recent reports, every previous major Bitcoin bear market saw prices fall below the realized price before bottoming out. Reaching that level would require a further 7.4% decline from Wednesday's reported low, as investors confront the prospect of tighter monetary policy and a prolonged withdrawal of institutional capital.

COLDCARD bug goes undetected for 5 years despite 15 security reviews: Details

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coinkite, the organization behind Bitcoin [BTC] hardware wallet COLDCARD, has revealed that a security vulnerability remained undetected for more than five years, despite at least 15 independent security reviews, including AI-assisted research.
  • According to the 23rd November, 2026 postmortem published by Coinkite, the issue affected certain COLDCARD firmware versions released between 29th March, 2021, and 30th July, 2026.
  • Although the devices continued to generate valid recovery phrases and appeared to function normally, an underlying firmware error meant that the randomness used to create private keys was weaker than intended.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinkite, the organization behind Bitcoin [BTC] hardware wallet COLDCARD, has revealed that a security vulnerability remained undetected for more than five years, despite at least 15 independent security reviews, including AI-assisted research.

According to the 23rd November, 2026 postmortem published by Coinkite, the issue affected certain COLDCARD firmware versions released between 29th March, 2021, and 30th July, 2026.

Although the devices continued to generate valid recovery phrases and appeared to function normally, an underlying firmware error meant that the randomness used to create private keys was weaker than intended.

That remarked, the problem stemmed from a software integration error that caused certain Coldcard devices to use a weaker pseudo-random number generator instead of the intended hardware-based system.

Sources indicate that this generator produced less unpredictable recovery phrases, making it easier for attackers to guess the private keys and access customers’ Bitcoin. Although the recovery phrases appeared normal and passed some security tests, they did not offer the expected level of protection.

As a result, the vulnerability reportedly resulted in the theft of at least 1,789 BTC, worth approximately $114.7 million at the time. As of 18th November, Coinkite had received around 300 loss-related support tickets linked to 242 customer accounts. However, the actual number of victims could be higher.

That said, vulnerability significantly reduced the difficulty of reconstructing affected wallet seeds. According to Coinkite, the affected seeds had approximately 40 bits of effective entropy on Mk2 and Mk3 devices and 72 bits on Mk4, Mk5, and Q devices.

This was considerably weaker than the originally intended 128-bit security. This allowed attackers to use offline brute-force searches to reconstruct private keys and gain access to Bitcoin holdings without physically accessing the hardware wallets.

However, Coinkite did address the problem on 31st July and introduced additional security measures in August. Yet, it is still investigating the incident alongside law enforcement authorities and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

Industry observers note that up until now, the firm has not finalized a compensation proposal. Regardless, it has been advised that the affected customers must generate entirely new recovery phrases and transfer their Bitcoin to new wallets.

This is because simply updating the firmware will not secure previously compromised recovery phrases.

All of this coincided with Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warning that artificial intelligence could potentially discover mathematical shortcuts to break the cryptographic systems protecting crypto private keys.

At the same time, crypto security losses surged 55% to $1.18 billion in Q3 2026, up from $763.97 million in Q2, while reported breaches increased from 67 to 107.

In that, compromised suppliers, delayed patches, and unaudited components accounted for 77% of losses, highlighting risks beyond smart contract vulnerabilities. Lastly, smart contract flaws also caused $569.5 million in losses, while access control and operational failures contributed to another $477.6 million.

Morgan Stanley has disclosed its latest crypto-related holdings in a quarterly Form 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. According to the filing, the bank's U.S. equity portfolio was valued at around $1.96 trillion as of Sept. 30, up from $1.89 trillion at the end of June.

Most of the crypto-related positions in the filing are Bitcoin products and Bitcoin-linked stocks, and the bank also reported a small amount of XRP exposure through three spot exchange-traded funds.

The largest crypto-related position in the filing is Strategy (MSTR). Morgan Stanley held around 10.88 million MSTR shares worth about $1.67 billion at the end of September, up from 9.33 million shares at the end of the second quarter.

The bank also increased its position in BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) from 16.48 million to 19.52 million shares, and the IBIT stake was worth about $924 million as of Sept. 30.

Besides, Morgan Stanley reported 6.72 million units of its own Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust (MSBT), up from 2.57 million units at the end of June. In the second-quarter filing, the MSBT position was worth about $43.3 million. MSBT started trading on NYSE Arca in April, and it was the first spot Bitcoin ETF issued by a major U.S. bank.

Among crypto stocks, Morgan Stanley also held around 10.54 million Robinhood (HOOD) shares worth about $1.19 billion and 3.72 million Coinbase (COIN) shares worth about $694 million.

It has been revealed that morgan Stanley reported $116,097 in XRP ETF holdings as of Sept. 30. Franklin's XRP fund accounted for $111,885 of that amount, REX-Osprey's fund for $3,098, and the Bitwise XRP ETF for the remaining $1,114.

In a recent development, the bank held the same three funds at the end of June. In the second quarter, Morgan Stanley reported 6,715 shares of the Franklin fund, 255 shares of the REX-Osprey fund and 67 shares of the Bitwise fund. Before that, the bank's first-quarter filing indicated 1,700 shares of the Volatility Shares XRP ETF and 100 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF worth $15,488 in total.

On Wednesday, XRP was trading at around $0.908, down 2.23% over 24 hours, according to CoinMarketCap.

Morgan Stanley was one of seven banks that disclosed XRP-linked ETF holdings in third-quarter 13F filings. The positions of the seven banks totaled about $29.4 million as of Sept. 30, and Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo accounted for $27.21 million of that amount.

It has been revealed that goldman Sachs reported much larger XRP positions. The bank's XRP ETF holdings rose from $87 million in the second quarter to $144 million in the third quarter, and Goldman's crypto portfolio was worth around $2.64 billion in total.

#110300. France’s Senate Rejects Rule Forcing Bitcoin Holders to Declare Self-Custody Wallets
